how_it_works: A single vertical list of 5 numbered 'chapters' (01–05) reading top-to-bottom in reverse-chronological order, each a collapsed accordion header row (mono index + role/org + date range). Exactly one chapter is expanded at a time; clicking a header expands its body in place and collapses the previously open one (single-open accordion, like a table of contents that unfolds sections). A slim PROGRESS INDICATOR sits alongside — either (a) a thin vertical maroon (#8B2E2A) rail down the left of the number column whose FILL height maps to which chapter index is active / how far you've read (chapter 3 of 5 = 60% filled), or (b) a fixed thin reading-progress bar tied to overall scroll. There are TWO viable interaction models and the pattern name allows either: (1) CLICK ACCORDION — native disclosure, no scroll-jack: headers stay put, only the body height animates open/closed via the CSS grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr trick (no JS height measuring), and the progress rail advances by active-index; this is the recruiter-safe default. (2) SCROLL-LINKED HEIGHT — the section is pinned (ScrollTrigger pin:true) and vertical scroll scrubs a timeline that collapses the current chapter's body (height/opacity to 0) while the next chapter's number highlights and its body grows, with the progress rail scrubbed 0→1 across the pin length; stagger cascades chapter-by-chapter so it 'steps' as you scroll. Model (1) has zero scroll distance beyond content; model (2) needs a bounded pin (~ one extra viewport per chapter, e.g. end '+=400%' for 5 beats) and MUST cap total pin length so recruiters aren't trapped. In both, the number column + progress fill is the persistent spine; the expanding body is the only large-moving element.
visual_structure: One beat = a chapter row. Collapsed state (the high-scan resting state): a two-part header — LEFT a large mono chapter index (JetBrains Mono, '01' … '05', muted or maroon on active) doubling as the ordinal of the career step; RIGHT the role title (Fraunces, the anchor) with org on the same baseline (Inter) and a mono date range as an overline or trailing meta (e.g. '01 · Junior Clinical Data Scientist — nference · 2026—Present'). A 1px hairline divides rows. Expanded state adds the body beneath the header: 2–3 tight Inter bullets, an optional proof chip row (mono, e.g. '~90% test acc' for DEXTER CXR, 'oncology clinical-note extraction' for nference), and optional a single quiet accent for the clinical beat (AMC bedside → small ECG hairline glyph). The progress element: a thin vertical track hugging the number column, empty (paper/#EAE6DE) with a maroon fill whose height = active step / total; or a segmented variant where each of the 5 segments fills as its chapter is reached (matches the numbered-step metaphor better than a continuous bar). Beats do NOT morph into one another — they expand/collapse in their fixed slot, so the list length is the only thing that changes. For Madhavi the 5 beats map cleanly to 01–05 (nference FT / nference intern / AMC clinical intern / DEXTER ML intern / Animations Media ops); the nference FT+intern continuity can be one chapter with a promoted-from sub-line OR two adjacent chapters — keeping them separate is what justifies exactly 5 numbered steps. Generous whitespace, editorial-minimal; the number + hairline + progress fill are the only 'chrome'.
motion_recipe: Default (click accordion): NO GSAP needed for the open/close — animate the body with the CSS grid trick: panel { display:grid; grid-template-rows:0fr; transition:grid-template-rows .32s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) } and [data-open] { grid-template-rows:1fr }, with an inner wrapper { overflow:hidden; min-height:0 } (keep padding OFF the grid child so it collapses fully). Build on native <details>/<summary> or a button with aria-expanded/aria-controls for free keyboard + SR state. Progress rail fill: transition height/scaleY .3s on active-index change, OR pure-CSS scroll-driven for a page reading bar — animation: grow linear; animation-timeline: scroll(root block); @keyframes grow{from{transform:scaleX(0)}to{transform:scaleX(1)}} wrapped in @supports(animation-timeline:scroll()). Chapter number active color cross-fades (150–200ms). Scroll-linked variant (only if you want the 'steps on scroll' wow): gsap.timeline({scrollTrigger:{trigger:'.stepper',start:'top top',end:'+='+(n*100)+'%',scrub:1,pin:true,pinSpacing:true,anticipatePin:1,invalidateOnRefresh:true}}); per chapter tl.to(body,{height:0,opacity:0,duration:1}) then tl.to(nextBody,{height:'auto'…}) — but prefer animating a wrapper's autoAlpha + a maxHeight/grid proxy over raw height where possible, and drive progress rail with the same scrub. DO animate transform/opacity (and the grid-rows exception, which is composited well enough for a short list); DON'T animate width/top/left, DON'T infinitely pulse the ECG accent, DON'T scrub the body text itself, and DON'T pin without a hard cap on end (recruiter trap). Use gsap.matchMedia to gate the pin to (min-width:768px) and (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference); test with markers:true.
reduced_motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop every transition/scrub but keep the disclosure semantics. Accordion still opens/closes on click — just instantly (media query: .panel{transition:none}) — so the pattern's meaning (expand a chapter in place) fully survives. Progress rail renders as a static filled bar reflecting position (or is simply the numbered 01–05 sequence itself, which already communicates 'step N of 5' without motion). Never gate any career content behind an animation: a safe fallback is to render ALL chapters expanded (or at least the current role) as a plain reverse-chronological numbered list — index, role, org, date, bullets — so a reader with reduced motion or JS disabled still gets the whole journey top-to-bottom. If using the scroll-linked/pinned variant, disable the pin entirely under reduced-motion and fall back to the click (or all-open) accordion; the numbered spine + hairlines carry the structure statically.
brand_fit: HIGH (for the click-accordion model) / MEDIUM (for the pinned scroll-linked model). The numbered 01–05 chapter list is intrinsically editorial-minimal and 'quiet, high-scan' exactly as the brief asks: it reads like a table of contents / a typeset chapter list, leans entirely on the existing type system (JetBrains Mono indices + dates, Fraunces roles, Inter body), and needs zero new dependencies — the CSS grid-rows accordion + a CSS scroll() progress bar are dependency-free and reduced-motion-trivial. The maroon progress fill is a natural, restrained home for the #8B2E2A accent (a thin rail, not a color wash), and 5 content beats map perfectly to 01–05, giving the numbering real meaning rather than decoration. It's anti-slop: no purple SaaS glow, no full-screen takeover, no horizontal scrub. It also solves scannability better than most journey patterns because collapsed headers show role+org+date at a glance and recruiters can jump to any chapter. The reason it's not unconditionally HIGH: (a) the SCROLL-LINKED/pinned height variant risks scroll-jack and recruiter friction (a pinned accordion that only opens as you scroll can hide content and feel slow) — that variant drops to MEDIUM; (b) generic numbered steppers read as SaaS onboarding-wizard chrome (checkmarks, 'Step 1 of 5' pills, blue/emerald states) — must be re-skinned to editorial (serif roles, mono indices, maroon hairline, no checkmark/badge UI) to avoid looking like a form wizard. Kept as a click accordion with a quiet maroon progress rail, it's one of the strongest fits.
steal: Steal the NUMBERED chapter index (01–05) fused with a thin maroon progress rail whose fill height = active step / 5, sitting in the left number column. Even on a plain click-accordion (or an all-open static list), that single mono ordinal + hairline-thin maroon fill turns a resume list into a legible 'career in 5 chapters' with a built-in sense of progress and place — for near-zero cost, no scroll-jack, and it doubles as the anchor for the one signature ECG accent on the AMC clinical chapter.
avoid: Avoid the SaaS onboarding-wizard skin and the pinned scroll-jack trap. Concretely: don't use checkmark badges, 'Step 3 of 5' pills, locked/greyed 'upcoming' states, or blue/emerald status colors — that reads as a form wizard, not a career story, and signals a copied component. And if you take the scroll-linked-height route, don't pin the section without a hard, short cap and a way out: a pinned accordion that hides each chapter's content until the user scrolls far enough is recruiter-hostile (they can't skim, can't jump, back-scroll re-triggers). Keep every chapter's role/org/date visible in the collapsed header at all times, keep at least the current role's body open by default, and never bury experience content behind a required scroll or animation.
live_examples: shadcn.io/blocks/stepper-accordion-expand — the canonical 'accordion-style stepper where the active step expands to reveal content while completed/upcoming stay collapsed' (React/Next/shadcn/Tailwind); read it for structure but RE-SKIN heavily (it's a form-wizard aesthetic, wrong palette). shadcn.io/blocks/stepper-vertical-numbered — vertical numbered circles connected by progress lines with expandable step content and completion tracking (closest to the 01–05 + progress-line metaphor).
